note: Rewritten from Emerson 1959, original in English (American Museum Novitates No. 1947: The African Termite Genera Firmitermes, Hoplognathotermes, Acutidentitermes, Duplidentitermes, and Heimitermes). The new species is described from a single soldier holotype (no worker), collected on 1948-5-20 by A. Emerson in an underground gallery at Pygmy Camp on the Epulu River, Belgian Congo (4 km north of Camp Putnam, 1°24′N, 28°36′E), and deposited in the American Museum of Natural History; the author notes that the tips of the mandibles of this specimen are broken. The whole original description is given in the form of comparisons with two congeners, and the absolute measurements are taken from TABLE 7 (a three-column comparison table), of which only the D. latimentonis column is recorded here; in the table the two entries "apex to inside tip of first marginal tooth" for the left and right mandible are given as "—" (not measurable) for this species and are not recorded. The outline of the postmentum in fig. 7E is not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared directly with the paratype soldier of D. furcatidens (Sjöstedt): the body colour and pilosity of the present species are similar; the projections on the head above the base of the mandibles and in front of the antennal bases are weaker, and the profile is flatter and less concave; the concavity at the front of the head is not as sharp as in D. jurioni. The postmentum is wider at both its widest and its narrowest point than in D. furcatidens and D. jurioni; in profile the convexity in the middle of the postmentum is slightly less than in D. furcatidens, and the posterior region has no transverse ridge or groove; the constriction of the postmentum is distinctly deeper than in D. jurioni. The base of the mandibles is slightly stouter than in D. furcatidens and the dentition similar; the pronotum is close to D. furcatidens, its anterior incision slightly sharper than in D. jurioni. The shape and pilosity of the fore coxa resemble D. jurioni; the tibial spurs and spines resemble those of the two species named above.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The description is given as a comparison with two congeners: the colour and pilosity are close to D. furcatidens; the projections on the front of the head (above the base of the mandibles and in front of the antennal bases) are weaker, and the profile is flatter and less concave; the postmentum is wider at both its widest and its narrowest point, with a distinct constriction, and its posterior region has no transverse ridge or groove; the antennae are broken off, and the relative proportions of the first 5 segments are as in D. furcatidens; the base of the mandibles is slightly stouter and the dentition the same, except that the tips of the mandibles are broken in the holotype; the pronotum is close to D. furcatidens, with the anterior incision slightly sharper; the fore coxa, tibial spurs and spines are as in D. jurioni. Measurements (holotype soldier, mm): head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 2.74; head width 2.11; head height 1.62; postmentum length 1.52; maximum width of the postmentum 0.89; minimum width of the postmentum 0.54; labrum width 0.71; length of the left mandible 1.47; pronotum length 0.79; pronotum width 1.44; hind tibia length 1.65.
